::: {.callout-tip}
## Why This Matters
China's leading DRAM maker (long known as Innotron/Hefei Chang Xin before its current name), majority state-controlled via Hefei SASAC and the Big Fund, now the world's fourth-largest DRAM producer by capacity.
:::

**Chinese name:** 长鑫存储 (Chángxīn Cúnchǔ)

## What does this facility make?

DRAM chips on 12-inch (300mm) wafers, now including DDR5-capable products.

## Why does it matter?

DRAM has been China's slower memory story relative to YMTC's NAND — CXMT's rise to fourth-largest globally by 2026 marks a real capability jump, arriving alongside a June 2026 US Department of Defense listing as a Chinese military-linked entity (distinct from, and less restrictive than, the Commerce Department's Entity List).

## Technology Node Trajectory

- **2020**: 19nm-class DRAM
- **2025**: DDR5-capable node (exact process width not disclosed)

## Project Timeline

- **01 May 2016** — Founded as Innotron Memory / Hefei Chang Xin
- **01 Jan 2017** — $7.2 billion investment announced for a 125,000 wafer/month 12-inch DRAM fab
- **01 Jun 2026** — Added to the US Department of Defense's list of Chinese military-linked companies (Section 1260H)
